name: Effective Range / Proper Stable Sample Compression
details: False for finite classes: #classes/balanced_six_split has effective range 10 and psUSC $+\infty$, because no proper unlabeled scheme exists at any size. Hence no finite-valued function of effective range is a universal upper bound. Retaining all active labeled examples proves the labeled analogue only. If a proper stable unlabeled scheme does exist, discarding constant coordinates yields size at most effective range; see survey Remark rem:proper-unlabeled-existence. The failure is therefore one of existence, not a larger finite size.
proof_source: Survey Corollary cor:balanced-six-split-nonexistence and Remark rem:proper-unlabeled-existence.
witness_verification: Values 1181 and 1185 give $E=10$ and psUSC $+\infty$. Nonexistence on a fixed finite class refutes every finite upper bound, not merely an affine one; this is not an asymptotic-family claim.
witness_review: The previous singletons-plus-empty witness has E=n and psUSC=1 and remains a valid gap in the opposite direction. It did not refute this inequality; the six-split class is the counterexample to the stated relation.
